name: video-adlikely
note: ROUND 19 CONTRACT (operator UAT 2026-09-17). This scenario owns the REMEMBERED PREFERENCE (music.vidPref.v1); video-pip.json owns the visible FORM. The two have swapped form twice now, which is exactly why they are split: round 17 opened a fresh play as the THEATER, round 18 (PR #342) demoted it to the corner PIP to stop it eating taps, and round 19 restores the theater WITH a scrim so it announces itself instead. Through all three the PREFERENCE contract below never changed, and that is the point of this file. What round 19 DOES change here is which control parks the video, because the park handle belongs to whichever form is on screen: a theater parks with [data-thmin] (its own down-arrow), a docked PIP parks with [data-piphide] (the slim tab on its left edge). This scenario taps [data-thmin] again, as it did before round 18. THE INVARIANTS: a fresh device shows the video (round 16's law - the Skip surface is never hidden unasked) and writes NOTHING; PARKING is a user act and IS remembered; a later open HONORS the park with no re-tap; showing it again flips the memory back; and a QUEUE ADVANCE carries the parked state - round 19 raises a theater on every new song EXCEPT a parked one, so 'hid' is the single standing choice that survives a song change. Docking a theater to the PIP via the scrim is deliberately NOT remembered (it is a this-song dismissal) - video-pip.json guards that half.

steps.label: ROUND 16's LAW ON A FRESH DEVICE (no stored preference) -> the video is VISIBLE, so the ad Skip surface is reachable without hunting. Asserted by VISIBILITY, not by a form class: a mini player shows the corner PIP, the open sheet shows the theater - the law is that the app never hides it on its own, not that it picks one particular card.
and nothing has been written to the preference yet - restoring a default must not masquerade as a user choice

PARKING IS A USER ACT -> it is remembered ('hid'), and the player wears the parked class. The theater's own down-arrow is the park control while a theater is the form on screen (round 19); [data-piphide] is the same act from a docked PIP.
THE NEXT OPEN HONORS IT - parked stays parked with no re-tap (round 15's quiet state, now owned by the user instead of hardcoded)
SHOWING IT AGAIN IS ALSO REMEMBERED - the preference flips back to theater, so the pendulum swings both ways
park it again mid-session (a user act, so it is remembered)

ROUND 17 - QUEUE ADVANCE WHILE PLAYING IS MID-SESSION: the next song CARRIES the parked state - the video must not jump up between songs (ads are unlikely here, and a jumping video is the friction this rule exists to avoid)
